cancer_indication: HER2-overexpressing (HER2+) breast cancer in both early (adjuvant/neoadjuvant) and metastatic settings.
moa: Trastuzumab binds the extracellular domain of the HER2 (ERBB2) receptor on tumor cells, causing receptor downmodulation and blockade of downstream signaling. This inhibits proliferative pathways (MAPK/ERK, PI3K/AKT) and induces cell-cycle arrest (including via p27^Kip1 upregulation). Through its Fc region, it recruits immune effector mechanisms by engaging Fcγ receptors on immune cells to mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against HER2+ tumor cells. It has also been shown to inhibit tumor angiogenesis.

REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.description: Represents oncogenic HER2 (ERBB2) receptor signaling driven by HER2 overexpression/amplification, including receptor activation and downstream proliferative/survival signaling outputs.
REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.interpretation: HER2-driven signaling is a key dependency in HER2-amplified breast cancer and is the central disease driver that trastuzumab targets at the receptor level.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core survival and growth signaling axis downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases, integrating PI3K, AKT, and mTOR activity to promote proliferation and resistance to cell death.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity is a major determinant of tumor survival in HER2+ breast cancer and is highlighted as a critical bypass/resistance axis when it remains active despite HER2 blockade.

KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Mitogenic signaling cascade (RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK) that transduces growth factor receptor inputs into transcriptional programs that drive proliferation and differentiation.
KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: MAPK signaling functions as a major HER2-linked growth pathway supporting tumor proliferation; sustained MAPK signaling is noted as a contributor to reduced response.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Gene program reflecting E2F-driven transcription required for S-phase entry and DNA replication, typically downstream of RB phosphorylation and cell-cycle progression.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F target activity serves as a proliferation readout in HER2+ tumors; trastuzumab’s anti-proliferative effects are linked to cell-cycle arrest and reduced proliferation-associated gene expression.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programs governing intrinsic and extrinsic apoptotic signaling that execute regulated cell death through caspase activation and death receptor/mitochondrial pathways.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptotic competence is relevant to HER2 blockade because trastuzumab can sensitize HER2+ tumor cells to apoptotic death, whereas anti-apoptotic signaling is described in resistant states.

GOBP_FC_GAMMA_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Immune effector signaling initiated by Fcγ receptor engagement on immune cells, triggering activation cascades that promote antibody-dependent cytotoxic and phagocytic responses.
GOBP_FC_GAMMA_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Fcγ receptor signaling underlies trastuzumab’s immune mechanism (ADCC) and is described as an important component of effective tumor clearance in HER2+ disease.

KEGG_NATURAL_KILLER_CELL_MEDIATED_CYTOTO.description: NK cell activation and cytotoxic effector mechanisms (including perforin/granzyme-mediated killing) that eliminate antibody-opsonized target cells.
KEGG_NATURAL_KILLER_CELL_MEDIATED_CYTOTO.interpretation: NK-mediated cytotoxicity is mechanistically tied to trastuzumab-driven ADCC and is described as correlating with response when robust immune activation is present.

HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.description: Gene program reflecting angiogenic signaling and neovascularization processes that support tumor perfusion, growth, and progression.
HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.interpretation: Angiogenesis is described as a tumor-supportive process that can be inhibited by trastuzumab and may counteract therapy when high.

HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING.description: Developmental signaling pathway controlling cell fate, stemness, and survival via NOTCH receptor activation and downstream transcriptional programs.
HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING.interpretation: Notch signaling is described as a compensatory survival/stemness pathway that can increase after HER2 blockade and contribute to resistance biology.

HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.description: Cytokine-driven signaling axis in which IL-6 activates JAK kinases and STAT3 transcriptional programs that promote inflammation, survival, and immune regulation.
HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.interpretation: IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling is described as implicated in resistance and survival programs (often linked with Notch/STAT3 and inflammatory signaling) in the trastuzumab context.

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: Phenotypic transition program involving loss of epithelial features and gain of mesenchymal traits, associated with invasiveness, stem-like behavior, and therapy resistance.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation: EMT is described as linked to a stem-like, trastuzumab-resistant phenotype and is noted as relevant even if not a direct trastuzumab target pathway.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High FCGR3A (CD16) expression on NK cells is stated to correlate with trastuzumab sensitivity, consistent with effective ADCC as a key mechanism.
p27^Kip1 (CDKN1B) upregulation is described as enforcing G1 arrest after trastuzumab exposure; baseline association with response is noted via CDK inhibitor/apoptotic context.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Activating mutations in PIK3CA are stated to reactivate PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of HER2 and confer trastuzumab resistance.
STAT3-mediated survival/anti-apoptotic signaling is described as becoming upregulated in resistant contexts (often linked to Notch/inflammatory signaling).
Notch signaling (including Notch1) is described as a compensatory pathway that can increase after HER2 blockade and promote survival/stemness and resistance.
Jagged1 (JAG1) is described as part of a Jagged1/Notch1 axis that can become upregulated following HER2 blockade and contribute to resistance biology.
Activation of HER3 (ERBB3) is described as providing bypass proliferative/survival signaling that can undermine trastuzumab effects.
Increased signaling through EGFR is described as an alternate receptor tyrosine kinase input that can provide bypass growth signals and contribute to resistance.
IGF1R signaling is described as a bypass pathway that can engage alternate proliferation/survival signals and reduce trastuzumab effectiveness.
SRC kinase signaling is described as frequently upregulated in resistant cells as part of bypass/survival signaling downstream of RTK cross-talk.
IL-6/JAK-STAT signaling is described as implicated in resistance and survival/inflammatory programs (linked to Notch/STAT3 context).
MET is described as a growth factor cross-talk RTK whose increased signaling can engage bypass pathways that undermine trastuzumab effects.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of PTEN is stated to reactivate PI3K/AKT signaling and confer trastuzumab resistance.
Resistant cells are described as often losing p27 (CDKN1B), allowing cell-cycle progression despite trastuzumab-associated arrest mechanisms.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive (ERBB2-amplified) Breast C: Trastuzumab is effective only in tumors overexpressing HER2 (approx. 15–20% of breast cancers). It improves outcomes in both hormone receptor–positive (often “Luminal B HER2+”) and hormone receptor–negative HER2+ tumors.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Negative Subtypes (TNBC, Luminal A/: Trastuzumab is not indicated because the target is absent. Clinical trials show no benefit in pure HER2-negative disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-Mutated Cancers: There is no specific role for trastuzumab based on BRCA status. HER2+ cancers should be treated with HER2-targeted therapy regardless of BRCA, and BRCA-mutant TNBC are managed with platinum/PARP inhibitors rather than trastuzumab.

notes: No absolute contraindications were stated; key safety issues described include cardiotoxicity (LVEF decline/heart failure risk), infusion reactions, embryo-fetal toxicity, and pulmonary toxicity.
